items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I had never seen Long-Haired Bob play. But they told me about him.

ctx.x: You'd go on the riverfront, where I'm going to take you this week, and you'd see the camps on the riverfront, on the stilts, like you see in an Oriental country. There were camps out there. It was just loaded with camps, and every camp on a Sunday had some kind of a music. And they went out to play out on a picnic; they'd have a picnic at such-and-such a camp, at Little Woods or Milenburg or West Bend or Seabrook, all along there -- each two or three miles there was a little village. And there was music, and…

My stepfather told me one day... I saw this guy when I was with my uncle. He said, "That's a trumpet player." I said, "How do you know?" He said, "Well, you see his lip? He's got a red lip spot on his lip." So I said, "You don't have to be a trumpet player..." No, a cornet player. "He don't have to be a cornet player because he's got a red spot on his lip." So I criticized(?) my stepfather. He said, "It might not, but he's a trumpet player." I said, "Who is he?" He said, "That's Long-Haired Bob."
